hints: The equations are over the field modulo 1,000,000,007, so arithmetic must use modular residues.
Use Gaussian elimination: find a nonzero pivot in each variable column, scale it to 1, and eliminate that variable from other rows.
A zero-coefficient row with nonzero right side means no solution; otherwise set free variables to zero and solve pivot variables.
analogy: Eliminate variables from the modular equations one column at a time, just as with ordinary linear algebra, but use modular inverses instead of division.
example: Modulo 7, equations x+y=3 and x-y=1 have solution x=2,y=1 because both equations hold modulo 7.
algorithm: Perform row-reduced Gaussian elimination on the augmented n by (m+1) matrix modulo MOD. For each column, find a nonzero pivot, swap it into place, multiply the row by pivot^(MOD-2), and eliminate that column from all other rows. Reject any row [0,...,0|nonzero]. Set nonpivot variables to 0 and read pivot variables from the reduced rows.
correctness: All row swaps, nonzero scaling, and row additions are invertible operations over the prime field and preserve the solution set. A contradictory zero row is exactly inconsistency; otherwise assigning free variables zero yields a valid solution.
